Fixes #27379

However by following the philosophy https://huggingface.co/blog/transformers-design-philosophy I decided to copy the model and view it as an independent addition

Perhaps @ArthurZucker has some insights here. It's also unclear to me whether this method allows for a new `model_type` or whether it should keep using the same `model_type` of the model you're taking the diff from

Hi @NielsRogge, the command for diff method seems to work fine if the `drop_path` function (copied from beit) in Dinov2 is changed to a method of `Dinov2DropPath` class, removing the "Copied from" statements.

Side Note:
Since the Beit drop_path implementation is directly used in many other models, similar issues may arise in the future unless the one in Beit is modified. Incidentally, FlaxBeitDropPath is coded correctly, in a single class, and this class is directly copied in FlaxDinov2.

````
class Dinov2DropPath(nn.Module):
    """Drop paths (Stochastic Depth) per sample (when applied in main path of residual blocks)."""

    def __init__(self, drop_prob: Optional[float] = None) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.drop_prob = drop_prob

    def drop_path(self, input: torch.Tensor, drop_prob: float = 0.0, training: bool = False) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Drop paths (Stochastic Depth) per sample (when applied in main path of residual blocks).

        Comment by Ross Wightman: This is the same as the DropConnect impl I created for EfficientNet, etc networks,
        however, the original name is misleading as 'Drop Connect' is a different form of dropout in a separate paper...
        See discussion: https://github.com/tensorflow/tpu/issues/494#issuecomment-532968956 ... I've opted for changing the
        layer and argument names to 'drop path' rather than mix DropConnect as a layer name and use 'survival rate' as the
        argument.
        """
        if drop_prob == 0.0 or not training:
            return input
        keep_prob = 1 - drop_prob
        shape = (input.shape[0],) + (1,) * (input.ndim - 1)  # work with diff dim tensors, not just 2D ConvNets
        random_tensor = keep_prob + torch.rand(shape, dtype=input.dtype, device=input.device)
        random_tensor.floor_()  # binarize
        output = input.div(keep_prob) * random_tensor
        return output

    def forward(self, hidden_states: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        return self.drop_path(hidden_states, self.drop_prob, self.training)

    def extra_repr(self) -> str:
        return "p={}".format(self.drop_prob)
```
